title: Maps from an ideal power lift modulo principal maps over a flat neighbourhood
statement: Let R and S be commutative rings and S an R-algebra with flat structure map. Let I be a finitely generated ideal of R such that R/I -> S/IS is an isomorphism, let n >= 1, and let N be an R-module. For every R-linear map d : I^n -> S tensor_R N, there exist an R-linear map l : I^n -> N and m in S tensor_R N such that 1 tensor l(r) = d(r) + r m for every r in I^n. Scalar extension is as in [def-weil-module-base-change] and flatness as in [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

source.place: Tag 05EG, second paragraph, the two right arrows of the diagram, with Tags 05ED, 05EE, 05EF, 05E9, 05EC; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05EG

proof.text: Choose a finite generating set s of J = I^n using Ideal.FG.pow. For any coefficient module P define the difference map delta : P^s -> P^(s x s), delta(z)_(i,j) = f_i z_j - f_j z_i. Let Z = ker delta, b : P -> Z send p to (f_i p), and H = Z / range b. The cycle equations show f_i [z] = 0, since f_i z = b(z_i); span induction shows J H = 0. This is the explicit homology computation of 05EF, including empty s.

For the cycle x_i = d(f_i), invert the finite-product tensor equivalence to obtain E.symm(x). Tensor induction computes the tensored difference map, so E.symm(x) belongs to its kernel. Flat exactness for Z -> P^s -> P^(s x s) gives t in S tensor Z mapping to E.symm(x). The torsion-module comparison of 05E9 applied to H, killed by I^n with n positive, lifts (S tensor q)(t) to h in H. Choose y in Z representing h. Flat exactness for P -> Z -> H gives m in S tensor P whose image equals 1 tensor y - t. Mapping into finite tuples proves 1 tensor y_i = x_i + f_i m. All quotient and tensor constructions are Mathlib constructions; no homology base-change equivalence needs a separate definition.

Let a : R^(s) -> J send a coefficient vector to its linear combination of the generators and b : R^(s) -> N send it to its linear combination of y_i. The generator equations give c b = (d + p_m) a, where c(z) = 1 tensor z and p_m(r) = r m. If a(z) = 0, then f_i b(z) = a(z) y_i = 0 by the cycle equations; span induction gives J b(z) = 0. Thus b(z) belongs to the I-power torsion submodule of N, and c(b(z)) = 0. Injectivity of the torsion-submodule base-change comparison of 05EC(1) forces b(z) = 0. This directly checks the relation images instead of constructing the naive Koszul quotient and applying the Hom comparison to its kernel.

The span of s is J, so the linear-combination map a is surjective. The proved inclusion ker a <= ker b allows b to descend to the quotient by ker a. Compose this descended map with the inverse of Mathlib LinearMap.quotKerEquivOfSurjective to obtain l : J -> N. Every element of J is a(z); the identity c b = (d + p_m) a yields 1 tensor l(r) = d(r) + r m for every r. Empty s, zero ideal, unit ideal, and zero coefficient module require no extra assumptions.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_ideal_power_hom_lift
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    (hflat : (algebraMap R S).Flat) (I : Ideal R) (hI : I.FG)
    (hquot : Function.Bijective
      (Ideal.quotientMap (I.map (algebraMap R S)) (algebraMap R S) Ideal.le_comap_map))
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    {N : Type w} [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
    (d : ↥(I ^ n) →ₗ[R] S ⊗[R] N) :
    ∃ (l : ↥(I ^ n) →ₗ[R] N) (m : S ⊗[R] N),
      ∀ r : ↥(I ^ n), 1 ⊗ₜ[R] l r = d r + (r : R) • m
